text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Serbian government adopts amendments to the income tax law and submits it to parliament.
- Visiting Moldovan Foreign Minister Mihay Popov and his Yugoslav counterpart Milan Milutinovic sign a protocol on cooperation between two foreign ministries.
- The Council of Europe will send observers for the upcoming local elections in Croatia.
- Belgrade-based committee for protection of rights of displaced persons protests to Croatia over organised settlement of Bosnian Croats in the Croatian Krajina region from which Serbs fled in 1995.
- Macedonia's car and tractors parts factory Ruen 1997 exports to Serbia to be worth seven million German marks.
- Kosovo Albanian side's expected insistence on independent Kosovo at the upcoming talks with the Serbian side in New York will blocks negotiations, commentary from Kosovo.
- Medicine supply will be normalised by the end of the month, says Serbian health minister Leposava Milicevic.
- Tender for radio and TV frequencies to be called in mid-April, says Serbian information minister Radmila Milentijevic.
NASA BORBA
- Serbian parliament finance committee accepts the final report on the 1996 budget at 10.2 billion dinars short of the planned 12 billion dinars.
- The Civil Alliance of Serbia, one of the Zajedno coalition partners, supports candidacy of Serbian Renewal Movement President Vuk Draskovic for Serbian presidential elections.
- Belgrade confectionary factory Soko Stark has exported to the value of $4.02 million in the first three months this year, 86 percent more than in the same period last year.
- Spokesman of the Socialist party of Serbia Ivica Dacic denies he will attend Serbia-Kosovo Albanian talks in New York.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- The Independent Serb Democratic Party from eastern Slavonia headed by its president Vojislav Stanimirovic has submitted its candidacy for the upcoming local elections in Croatia.
- The International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies says it will try to keep soup kitchens in Yugoslavia open until autumn.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Serbia needs 1.2 billion dinars each month to pay out pensions, but the pension fund collects only 800 million.
- Large quantities of cigarettes, certain oil derivatives and coffee cross into Serbia without duties.
- Representatives of the International Committee of the Red Cross try to fabricate proof about torture of Kosovo Albanians in Pristina prison by soliciting "testimony" from an inmate.
BORBA

- Serbian power company Elektroprivreda Srbije's claims from consumers have grown to 1.87 million dinars, and debts to 1.7 million dinars. Increase in prices and exports of electricity seen as way out of difficult situation.

- Priboj truck factory FAP to export 1.3 million German marks worth of truck components to Italy this year. Deals for exports to Germany concluded, negotiations under way with China for exports of buses.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Police minister Filip Vujanovic denies Belgrade daily Blic report that the general manager of Montenegro's aluminum plant Danilo Vuksanovic had fled with a bag full of two million German marks.
- Italy is interested in buying complete production of the Danilovgrad marble factory.
- Three Montenegrin funds sold 10 companies to new owners. Montenegro's privatisaiton plan includes 110 companies worth 370 million German marks.
- There are around 140 AIDS-infected people in Montenegro according to estimates.
MONITOR
- More than a third of the cabinet of Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic, plus two out of his three deputies, are loyal to President Momir Bulatovic.
- Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic cannot win easily and his only chance is for Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to accept a kind of truce, commentary.

- This is a struggle between rival clans as well as a struggle between different concepts, says Srdjan Darmanovic in an article about Montenegrin opposition views of the conflict within the ruling party.
- Independence is the most important issue for the future of Montenegro, says Dragan Hajdukovic, the creator of the idea Montenegro as an ecological state, in a letter to president Momir Bulatovic.
